title: Georgia Savannah designated uses and original assessed-water geography
scope: Complete publisher Savannah basin; original217 membership is a separate geometric intersection.

relationships.evidence: Both sources end at Carters Creek and publish Drinking Water. Legal start is Little Beaverdam Creek; assessment start is the North & South Beaverdam confluence. Resolve those distinct named starts before assigning the full legal reach.
Second published interval continues McIntosh Creek to Fitz Branch. The legal source says Fitz Creek, so the endpoint name difference remains explicit.
First published interval starts at legal Walnut Branch and ends at McIntosh Creek.
Both sources start at Comer Carlton Rd. (Athens Hwy). Assessment ends at South Fork Broad; legal source ends at Mill Branch.
Both sources end at Scull Shoal Creek. Source start SR 281 is not automatically equated with legal Wildcat Bridge Rd.

Assessment Stateline to West Fork Chattooga River corresponds in text to the legal GA–NC state line to West Fork interval. Original generic Stateline label, newline and trailing quote remain preserved.
Both original descriptions run from West Fork Chattooga River to Tugaloo Reservoir / Lake Tugaloo; both publish recreation plus wild/scenic uses.
Assessment publishes Tugalo Lake, near Tallulah Falls. The legal record names Chattooga River/Tugaloo Reservoir; spelling and waterbody form are preserved.
Reservoir 59 to Reservoir 51; Drinking Water is published.
Reservoir 51 to Hickory Level Creek; matches the legal downstream landmark and publishes Drinking Water.

features.source_name: A.H. Stephens State Park Group Camp Beach

relationships.evidence: Published A.H. Stephens group camp beach references Federal Lake. A beach feature and complete lake polygon have different geographic support.

features.source_name: Federal Lake (Previously known as Liberty Lake)

relationships.evidence: The actual publisher Name explicitly states Federal Lake (Previously known as Liberty Lake), with A.H. Stephens State Park location.
Reservoir 30 to Beaverdam Creek; actual assessment Uses is Fishing while legal record declares Drinking Water.
Headwaters to Reservoir 30; actual assessment Uses is Fishing while legal record declares Drinking Water.
Published Drinking Water interval runs Unawatti Creek to Broad River near Carnesville. Legal interval runs Double Branch to Middle Fork Broad River.
Clarks Hill Lake is expressly named in the legal record; the polygon has Drinking Water/Recreation/Fishing uses.
Richard B. Russell Lake is the Savannah-basin reservoir component; retain full actual Name and ReachID.
Stevens Creek Dam to Horse Creek forms the lower named river interval; its source also retains the former US 78/278 endpoint note.
Clarks Hill Dam to Stevens Creek Dam forms the upper named river interval.
Johnsons Landing to Brier Creek is a Drinking Water interval; the legal upstream US 301 landmark is not inferred from it.
Source retains literal Screnven/Effingham spelling and continues to Ebenezer Creek.
Brier Creek to Screven/Effingham County line is a published Drinking Water interval.
Ebenezer Creek to Railroad bridge upstream of Chatham County is a Drinking Water interval; original railroad wording is retained.
Railroad bridge to SR 25 is a published Coastal Fishing interval.
Savannah Harbor runs SR 25 (old US 17) to Elba Island Cut and publishes Coastal Fishing.
Source runs Pond at Corry Circle to South Fork Little River and publishes Drinking Water. Legal start is headwaters including Sherrills Reservoir.
Both original stream intervals run headwaters to Brier Creek and publish Drinking Water.
State line to Lake Burton is a published Recreation interval.
Burton Lake is explicitly named in the legal reach.
Seed (Nacoohe) Lake retains the original parenthetical name and is explicitly named as Lake Seed in the legal record.
Rabun Lake publishes Drinking Water/Recreation/Fishing and is explicitly named in the legal designation.
Tallulah Gorge Beach references Tallulah Falls; preserve separate beach support.
Original Name is Talulah Falls (one l), location near Tallulah Falls, Recreation/Fishing; retained as a candidate waterbody component.
Yonah Lake publishes Drinking Water/Recreation/Fishing and supplies a named component near the legal downstream dam.
Tugaloo State Park Beach lies on the published Hartwell Lake source; preserve its separate beach support.
Hartwell Lake original location is Tugaloo Arm/Main Body and publishes Drinking Water/Recreation/Fishing.
Published interval starts at Big Creek and ends at Chattooga River; Wild River/Scenic River uses agree with the legal components.
